articles.title: Crypto Market Data API or Trading API? Use a Feed for Prices, Not Orders
articles.excerpt: Does your crypto app need to show what the market is doing, or does it need to change something in an account? Use a market data API for the first job and a trading API for the second. The difference…
articles.body: Does your crypto app need to show what the market is doing, or does it need to change something in an account? Use a market data API for the first job and a trading API for the second. The difference is visible in exchange API documentation: a ticker returns a market observation, while a new-order endpoint submits an instruction to the exchange. A price alert can run without an order-capable credential. A bot that actually trades needs two separate paths: one for the signal and one for the order lifecycle. A live price tells you what happened in the market; the order and fill records tell you what happened to your account. Pick the interface by the side effect On Binance Spot, the market API documents a symbol price ticker separately from the trading API's signed new-order operation.

articles.title: Why your Shopify Payments payout never matches your sales, and how to book it
articles.excerpt: If you run a Shopify store and keep proper books, you have met this problem: you sold 1,240 EUR this week, and Shopify Payments wired you 1,187.32 EUR. The transfer matches no invoice and no daily tot…
articles.body: If you run a Shopify store and keep proper books, you have met this problem: you sold 1,240 EUR this week, and Shopify Payments wired you 1,187.32 EUR. The transfer matches no invoice and no daily total. Your accountant asks what it is, and you open the payout page in Shopify and start copying numbers. Here is how that payout actually breaks down, and how to book it so the bank reconciles to the cent. I'll use French accounting accounts as the example, but the logic is the same in any double-entry system. What a payout contains Shopify Payments groups several days of card payments into one bank transfer and subtracts a few things on the way: the processing fee on each order; the refunds issued during the period; disputes, reserves and adjustments, when there are any.

articles.title: We didn't feel comfortable giving our AI agent our API keys
articles.excerpt: My brother and I have been running AI agents for a few months now — Hermes-based agents that fetch things, send emails, touch GitHub, do real work while we do other things. Once an agent actually fini…
articles.body: My brother and I have been running AI agents for a few months now — Hermes-based agents that fetch things, send emails, touch GitHub, do real work while we do other things. Once an agent actually finishes a real task for you, it's hard to go back. Then comes the part nobody talks about. The agent needs to send Gmail: here's an app password. It needs GitHub: here's a personal access token. It needs to call the model: here's an API key. One by one we pasted live credentials into config files and hoped that nothing weird would ever show up in the context window. We kept asking ourselves the same question: what happens the day our agent gets lied to?

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Shakeup: China’s Chip Strategy Impact
articles.excerpt: Background For 33 years, Jensen Huang steered Nvidia from a niche graphics card maker into a global powerhouse that now powers gaming, data centers, autonomous vehicles, and AI workloads. In late 2025…
articles.body: Background For 33 years, Jensen Huang steered Nvidia from a niche graphics card maker into a global powerhouse that now powers gaming, data centers, autonomous vehicles, and AI workloads. In late 2025, Huang stepped down amid a swirl of controversies, including an alleged extramarital affair with a Chinese national and accusations of facilitating chip smuggling to China. Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO, and the company announced it would no longer sell its H200 AI accelerator to Chinese customers. The move stunned investors, with Nvidia’s market capitalization falling by roughly a trillion dollars. Over 200,000 tech executives, from Y Combinator to Shopify, signed a petition demanding Huang’s return. Despite his offer, Nvidia’s board has remained firm.

articles.title: Stop Renting, Start Owning. Build a Social Media site. It's the New Blog.
articles.excerpt: Building in public, part 3. Build your own, I'll show you how. If you're old enough, you remember having a blog. Blogger and LiveJournal both launched in 1999, and WordPress followed in May 2003. You…
articles.body: Building in public, part 3. Build your own, I'll show you how. If you're old enough, you remember having a blog. Blogger and LiveJournal both launched in 1999, and WordPress followed in May 2003. You picked a theme, wrote whatever you wanted, and people found you through RSS and blogrolls. It was small, but it was yours. Then most of us made a trade without really noticing. We moved our writing, our photos and our arguments onto platforms that had the audience. The deal was simple: they host it for free, and we get reach. This piece is about why that deal has gone bad, why AI has made the old idea of owning your space practical again, and how to actually do it.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 19, 2005: Japan's Hayabusa spacecraft makes 1st-ever liftoff from surface of an asteroid
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 19, 2005, the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft made the first liftoff from an asteroid. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 19, 2005, the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft made the first liftoff from an asteroid. Hayabusa was supposed to return asteroid samples to Earth. Asteroids are space rocks that were formed during the early solar system. We study asteroids to learn more about the solar system's history. Hayabusa (pronounced HI-uh-BOOS-uh) made two touchdowns on asteroid Itokawa (EE -toh-KA-wah). Each time, the spacecraft went into safe mode. Controllers weren't sure if Hayabusa gathered any material. But they sent the spacecraft back to Earth anyway. Hayabusa's sample return capsule returned to Earth in June 2010 . Scientists found dust of Itokawa inside the capsule, proving that it did indeed capture samples of Itokawa.

A new report from market research firm Circana shows that gamers were a bit more frugal this October than they were last year, despite two major games releasing that month. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launched on October 23, and Gears of War: E-Day released on October 1; both games enjoyed reasonable critical reception, though reviews for Modern Warfare 4 were rather mixed . articles.excerpt: Japan's space agency has decided to switch destinations and objectives for the final act of its Hayabusa2 asteroid mission, due to problems with the spacecraft's ion thrusters.
articles.body: Japan's space agency has decided to switch destinations and objectives for the final act of its Hayabusa2 mission, due to the spacecraft suffering trouble with its ion thrusters. The veteran Hayabusa2 spacecraft launched back in 2014 to collect material from the asteroid Ryugu . Since delivering the samples to Earth in December 2020 via a reentry capsule, the main spacecraft has been conducting an extended mission of exploration and in July made a super-close flyby of the two-headed asteroid Torifune. But Hayabusa2's continued adventures are now set for a premature end.

articles.title: China rolls out rocket for launch of 1st international astronaut to Tiangong space station (video)
articles.excerpt: China has rolled to the launch pad the rocket and spacecraft for its Shenzhou-24 mission, which will fly the first international astronaut to the nation's Tiangong space station.
articles.body: China's space station is set to receive its first foreign astronaut. A Long March 2F rocket, topped with the Shenzhou-24 crew spacecraft, was rolled out to the pad at Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, on Tuesday (Nov. 17), with launch expected in the next week. The 191-foot-tall (58 meters) rocket was transferred 0.93 miles (1.5 kilometers) from a vertical integration building to the pad over the course of around two hours, starting around 4 a.m. EST (0900 GMT, or 5 p.m. Beijing Time), according to China Central Television (CCTV). China rolls out the Long March 2F rocket for its Shenzhou-24 astronaut mission on Nov. 17, 2026.
